messages.author: 20758fda448fdbda
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] issue with neg_binomial_rng
parts:
I'm not sure this has anything to do with the problem, but I think the definition of the NB as listed in the manual is incorrect, unless a different parameterization is being used.

I believe the combinatorial prefix should be:
Choose(n + a - 1, a)

instead of:
Choose(n + a - 1, a - 1)

Thus, the logs should be:
lgamma(a + n) - lgmma(a + 1) - lgamma(n)

instead of:
lgamma(a + n) - lgmma(n + 1) - lgamma(a)

and the errors propagate to the gradient definitions.

If this is what is being programmed, that may be the source of some issues.

Avi

messages.author: 20758fda448fdbda
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] issue with neg_binomial_rng
parts:
On further review, it may well be that this could be due to R and Stan using different parameterizations. If Stan is actually following Gelman et al (2014 p. 44), then it is self consistent, but has defined successes and failures opposite that of R (check ?rbinom). Stan seems to be using alpha is the number of set failures for which we are finding the probability of y successes. R, on the other hand, has x as the random successes before a fixed number of n failures. In other words, "p" and (1-p) are reversed so that the exponent to the 1 / 1+ b and b / 1 + b have to be switched between the two.

Compare Wikipedia with Wolfram for an example where the exponents are "swapped" because of the definitions.

Linus, using your Stan parametrization, did you generate variates in R using size and mu?

Here's a minimal reproducible example:

require(rstan)

any ~ normal(0, 1);
}
generated quantities {
real y_correct[1000];
real y_incorrect[1000];

for (i in 1:1000) {
y_correct [i] <- poisson_rng (gamma_rng (shape, shape/mu));
}

for (i in 1:1000) {
y_incorrect [i] <- neg_binomial_rng(shape, shape/mu);
}
}', data=list(shape=4, mu=2))

as.matrix(fit) -> mfit
correct_sample <- mfit[, grep("y_correct", colnames(mfit))]
incorrect_sample <- mfit[, grep("y_incorrect", colnames(mfit))]

r_test <- rnbinom(1000, mu=2, size=4)

mean(correct_sample)
mean(incorrect_sample)
mean(r_test)
sd(correct_sample)
sd(incorrect_sample)
sd(r_test)
